questions.questionText: Statements: "All algorithms are instructions. All instructions are logic." Conclusions: I. All algorithms are logic. II. Some logic are algorithms.
questions.explanation: Universal affirmative Barbara syllogism: All A are B, All B are C => All A are C (Conclusion I follows). By conversion of universal affirmative, "Some C are A" also validly follows (Conclusion II follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "No compiler is an interpreter. Some translators are compilers." Conclusions: I. Some translators are not interpreters. II. All translators are interpreters.
questions.explanation: The translators that are compilers cannot be interpreters (since no compiler is an interpreter). Therefore, some translators are definitively not interpreters (Conclusion I follows). Conclusion II directly contradicts this.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only a few developers are managers. All managers are leaders." Conclusions: I. Some developers are leaders. II. All developers can never be managers.
questions.explanation: "Only a few developers are managers" implies both "Some developers are managers" and "Some developers are not managers". The developers who are managers are leaders (Conclusion I follows). "Only a few" strictly means that not all developers can be managers (Conclusion II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some databases are relational. No relational is NoSQL." Conclusions: I. Some databases are not NoSQL. II. All databases are NoSQL.
questions.explanation: The databases that are relational cannot be NoSQL (since no relational is NoSQL). Thus, those relational databases are not NoSQL (Conclusion I follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "All servers are machines. No machine is faultless." Conclusions: I. No server is faultless. II. Some machines are servers.
questions.explanation: Since all servers are inside the machine category, and no machine can be faultless, no server can be faultless (I follows). By conversion of "All servers are machines", some machines are servers (II follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some networks are secure. Some secure systems are encrypted." Conclusions: I. Some networks are encrypted. II. No network is encrypted.
questions.explanation: Two particular premises ("Some", "Some") yield no definite conclusion about the relationship between networks and encryption. However, Conclusions I ("Some") and II ("No") form an I-E complementary pair. Exactly one must be true.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All routers are hardware. Some hardware are switches." Conclusions: I. Some routers being switches is a possibility. II. All switches are routers.
questions.explanation: There is no negative premise restricting routers and switches. Hence an overlap between routers and switches is completely possible (Conclusion I follows). Conclusion II is an unproven definite claim.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No cat is a dog. No dog is a horse." Conclusions: I. No cat is a horse. II. Some horses are cats.
questions.explanation: Two universal negative premises ("No", "No") yield no valid syllogistic conclusion between extreme terms. Cats and horses could overlap or be disjoint. Neither definite conclusion follows.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All books are pages. All pages are words." Conclusions: I. All books are words. II. All words are books.
questions.explanation: Transitive inclusion: All Books -> Pages -> Words (I follows). The converse "All words are books" is an illicit universal conversion and does not follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only laptops are portables. Some laptops are powerful." Conclusions: I. All portables are laptops. II. Some portables are powerful.
questions.explanation: "Only laptops are portables" translates formally to "All portables are laptops" (Conclusion I follows). Whether portables specifically overlap with powerful laptops is unknown, so Conclusion II does not definitely follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some pens are pencils. Some pencils are markers." Conclusions: I. Some pens are markers. II. No pen is a marker.
questions.explanation: No definite conclusion can be drawn from two "Some" premises. But Conclusions I (Some) and II (No) form a complementary contradictory pair. Either I or II must follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All cars are vehicles. No vehicle is an airplane." Conclusions: I. No car is an airplane. II. No airplane is a car.
questions.explanation: All cars are inside vehicles, and vehicles have zero intersection with airplanes. Hence no car can be an airplane (I follows). Conversion of universal negative gives "No airplane is a car" (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Few students are athletes. Most athletes are energetic." Conclusions: I. Some students are energetic. II. Some students are athletes.
questions.explanation: "Few" means "Some". Thus "Some students are athletes" is directly given in the premise (Conclusion II follows). Transitive connection to energetic cannot be definitively asserted.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All mobile phones are gadgets. All gadgets are electronic. All electronics are useful." Conclusions: I. All mobile phones are useful. II. Some useful items are gadgets.
questions.explanation: A four-term transitive chain: Mobile -> Gadgets -> Electronic -> Useful. Therefore all mobiles are useful (I follows). By conversion, some useful items are gadgets (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some fruits are sweet. All sweet things are sugar." Conclusions: I. Some fruits are sugar. II. All sugar are fruits.
questions.explanation: Darii syllogism: Some fruits are sweet + All sweet are sugar => Some fruits are sugar (I follows). Universal converse does not follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No triangle is a circle. All circles are spheres." Conclusions: I. Some spheres are not triangles. II. Some spheres are circles.
questions.explanation: All circles are spheres, and no circle is a triangle. The spheres that are circles can never be triangles, so some spheres are not triangles (I follows). Conversion of "All circles are spheres" gives "Some spheres are circles" (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Every tree is a plant. No plant is mineral." Conclusions: I. No tree is mineral. II. Every mineral is a tree.
questions.explanation: All trees are plants, and plants have no overlap with minerals. Therefore, no tree can be mineral (I follows). Conclusion II is contradictory.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some integers are prime. All primes are positive." Conclusions: I. Some integers are positive. II. All positive numbers are prime.
questions.explanation: Some integers are prime, and all primes are positive => Those prime integers are positive (I follows). Conclusion II is an invalid converse generalization.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only a few roses are red. All red things are flowers." Conclusions: I. Some roses are not red. II. Some roses are flowers.
questions.explanation: "Only a few roses are red" explicitly implies that some roses are NOT red (I follows). The roses that are red are flowers, so some roses are flowers (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No plastic is biodegradable. Some packaging is plastic." Conclusions: I. Some packaging is not biodegradable. II. All packaging is biodegradable.
questions.explanation: The packaging made of plastic cannot be biodegradable. Therefore, some packaging is definitively not biodegradable (Conclusion I follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "All coders are thinkers. No thinker is reckless." Conclusions: I. No coder is reckless. II. Some thinkers are coders.
questions.explanation: All coders are thinkers; no thinker is reckless => No coder is reckless (I follows). Conversion of universal affirmative gives some thinkers are coders (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some doctors are surgeons. All surgeons are specialists." Conclusions: I. Some doctors are specialists. II. All specialists are surgeons.
questions.explanation: Doctors who are surgeons are specialists, so some doctors are specialists (I follows). The converse "All specialists are surgeons" is invalid.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No paper is plastic. All plastic is synthetic." Conclusions: I. Some synthetic are not paper. II. No paper is synthetic.
questions.explanation: All plastic is synthetic, and no paper is plastic. The synthetic items that are plastic cannot be paper, so some synthetic are not paper (I follows). Paper could still overlap with other non-plastic synthetics, so II does not follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All rivers are water bodies. All water bodies are essential." Conclusions: I. All rivers are essential. II. Some essential things are rivers.
questions.explanation: Barbara chain: Rivers -> Water bodies -> Essential (I follows). By conversion, some essential things are rivers (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only a few tests are easy. No easy thing is impossible." Conclusions: I. Some tests are impossible. II. Some tests are not impossible.
questions.explanation: Some tests are easy ("Only a few tests are easy"), and no easy thing is impossible. Therefore, those easy tests are not impossible (Conclusion II follows). Whether other tests are impossible is not definitively known.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some metals are heavy. All heavy things have mass." Conclusions: I. Some metals have mass. II. All things with mass are metals.
questions.explanation: Metals that are heavy have mass, so some metals have mass (I follows). II is an invalid over-generalization.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No bird is a fish. No fish is an insect." Conclusions: I. No bird is an insect. II. Some birds are insects.
questions.explanation: Two negative premises give no definite relation between birds and insects. However, "No bird is an insect" and "Some birds are insects" form an E-I contradictory pair. Therefore, either I or II must follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All apples are red. Some red things are sweet." Conclusions: I. Some apples being sweet is a possibility. II. Some apples are definitively sweet.
questions.explanation: Sweet things overlap with red things; apples are inside red things. An overlap between apples and sweet is possible (I follows), but cannot be definitely asserted (II does not follow).

questions.questionText: Statements: "Every diamond is carbon. Every carbon is an element." Conclusions: I. Every diamond is an element. II. Some elements are diamonds.
questions.explanation: Universal affirmative chain: Diamond -> Carbon -> Element (I follows). By conversion, some elements are diamonds (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only graduates are eligible. Some eligible people are experienced." Conclusions: I. All eligible people are graduates. II. Some graduates are experienced.
questions.explanation: "Only graduates are eligible" means "All eligible people are graduates" (I follows). Since some eligible people are experienced, and all eligible people are graduates, those experienced eligible people must be graduates (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some planets are rocky. No rocky body is a gas giant." Conclusions: I. Some planets are not gas giants. II. All planets are gas giants.
questions.explanation: The planets that are rocky cannot be gas giants. Hence some planets are not gas giants (I follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are polygons." Conclusions: I. All squares are polygons. II. Some polygons are squares.
questions.explanation: Squares -> Rectangles -> Polygons. Transitivity ensures all squares are polygons (I follows). Conversion yields some polygons are squares (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No hero is a coward. Some soldiers are cowards." Conclusions: I. Some soldiers are not heroes. II. All soldiers are heroes.
questions.explanation: The soldiers who are cowards cannot be heroes (since no hero is a coward). Therefore, some soldiers are not heroes (I follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "Few cars are electric. All electric vehicles are clean." Conclusions: I. Some cars are clean. II. All cars are clean.
questions.explanation: "Few" = "Some". Some cars are electric, and all electric are clean => Some cars are clean (I follows). Universal assertion II is invalid.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All trees have roots. All roots absorb water." Conclusions: I. All trees absorb water. II. Everything that absorbs water is a tree.
questions.explanation: Trees -> Roots -> Absorbs water (I follows). Converse II is an invalid illicit conversion.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some cloud servers are virtual. All virtual servers are scalable." Conclusions: I. Some cloud servers are scalable. II. All scalable servers are cloud servers.
questions.explanation: Cloud servers that are virtual are scalable => Some cloud servers are scalable (I follows). II is invalid.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only a few artists are famous. No famous person is ignored." Conclusions: I. Some artists are not famous. II. Some artists are not ignored.
questions.explanation: "Only a few artists are famous" entails some artists are not famous (I follows). The artists who are famous are not ignored, so some artists are not ignored (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All routers use IP. All switches use MAC." Conclusions: I. Some routers use MAC. II. No router uses MAC.
questions.explanation: There is no linking premise between IP and MAC. Thus the relationship between routers and MAC is unknown. However, Conclusions I (Some) and II (No) form an I-E contradictory pair, so either I or II must follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No predator is a plant. All tigers are predators." Conclusions: I. No tiger is a plant. II. No plant is a tiger.
questions.explanation: Tigers are inside predators, which are completely disjoint from plants. No tiger is a plant (I follows). Conversion gives no plant is a tiger (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some integers are odd. All odd integers end in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9." Conclusions: I. Some integers end in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9. II. All integers end in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9.
questions.explanation: Odd integers end in those digits; since some integers are odd, some integers end in those digits (I follows). Universal statement II is false.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All circles are curves. No curve is a straight line." Conclusions: I. No circle is a straight line. II. All straight lines are circles.
questions.explanation: Circles are curves; curves have zero overlap with straight lines => No circle is a straight line (I follows). II is completely contradictory.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only a few laptops are gaming machines. All gaming machines have GPUs." Conclusions: I. Some laptops have GPUs. II. Some laptops are not gaming machines.
questions.explanation: "Only a few" means some are and some are not (II follows). Laptops that are gaming machines have GPUs, so some laptops have GPUs (I follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some birds are swans. All swans are white." Conclusions: I. Some birds are white. II. All white things are birds.
questions.explanation: Birds that are swans are white => Some birds are white (I follows). II is an invalid illicit converse.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No star is a planet. No planet is a satellite." Conclusions: I. No star is a satellite. II. Some stars are satellites.
questions.explanation: Two negative premises yield no definite relation between stars and satellites. But "No" and "Some" are an E-I complementary pair, so either I or II follows.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All managers are employees. All employees are salaried." Conclusions: I. All managers are salaried. II. Some salaried persons are managers.
questions.explanation: Managers -> Employees -> Salaried (I follows). Conversion yields some salaried persons are managers (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only admins have root access. Some admins are remote." Conclusions: I. All people with root access are admins. II. Some remote users may have root access.
questions.explanation: "Only admins have root access" = "All people with root access are admins" (I follows). Since some admins are remote, it is entirely possible that some remote users have root access (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some metals are conductors. No conductor is an insulator." Conclusions: I. Some metals are not insulators. II. All metals are insulators.
questions.explanation: Metals that are conductors cannot be insulators => Some metals are not insulators (I follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "All roses are flowers. All flowers are beautiful." Conclusions: I. All roses are beautiful. II. Some beautiful things are roses.
questions.explanation: Roses -> Flowers -> Beautiful (I follows). Conversion yields some beautiful things are roses (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No triangle is a quadrilateral. All squares are quadrilaterals." Conclusions: I. No triangle is a square. II. No square is a triangle.
questions.explanation: Squares are quadrilaterals, which have zero overlap with triangles. No square is a triangle and no triangle is a square. Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Few books are novels. Most novels are fiction." Conclusions: I. Some books are fiction. II. Some books are novels.
questions.explanation: "Few" = "Some". Hence "Some books are novels" is directly given in premise (II follows). Fiction overlap cannot be definitely confirmed.

questions.questionText: Statements: "All dogs are animals. All animals need oxygen." Conclusions: I. All dogs need oxygen. II. Some organisms that need oxygen are dogs.
questions.explanation: Dogs -> Animals -> Need oxygen (I follows). Conversion gives some organisms that need oxygen are dogs (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some software are open source. No open source is proprietary." Conclusions: I. Some software are not proprietary. II. All software are proprietary.
questions.explanation: The software that are open source cannot be proprietary. Hence some software are not proprietary (I follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only a few phones are 5G. All 5G phones are fast." Conclusions: I. Some phones are fast. II. All phones are 5G.
questions.explanation: Some phones are 5G, and all 5G are fast => Some phones are fast (I follows). Conclusion II directly contradicts "Only a few".

questions.questionText: Statements: "All CPUs are processors. All processors are chips." Conclusions: I. All CPUs are chips. II. Some chips are CPUs.
questions.explanation: CPUs -> Processors -> Chips (I follows). Conversion yields some chips are CPUs (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No even number is odd. All multiples of 4 are even." Conclusions: I. No multiple of 4 is odd. II. No odd number is a multiple of 4.
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4 are inside evens, which have zero overlap with odds. Hence no multiple of 4 is odd, and vice versa. Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Some trees are tall. Some tall things are green." Conclusions: I. Some trees are green. II. No tree is green.
questions.explanation: Two "Some" premises yield no definite link between trees and green. However, Conclusions I (Some) and II (No) form an I-E contradictory pair. Either I or II must follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "Every citizen has rights. No right is unconditional." Conclusions: I. No citizen has unconditional rights. II. All citizens have unconditional rights.
questions.explanation: Citizens' rights are within the rights category; rights are never unconditional => No citizen has unconditional rights (I follows).

questions.questionText: Statements: "Only engineers are eligible for technical interview. Rahul is eligible for technical interview." Conclusions: I. Rahul is an engineer. II. Rahul is not an engineer.
questions.explanation: "Only engineers are eligible" = "All eligible people are engineers". Since Rahul is eligible, Rahul must be an engineer (Conclusion I follows definitively).

questions.questionText: Statements: "All planets have orbits. All orbits are elliptical." Conclusions: I. All planets have elliptical orbits. II. Some elliptical orbits belong to planets.
questions.explanation: Planets -> Orbits -> Elliptical (I follows). Conversion yields some elliptical orbits belong to planets (II follows). Both follow.

questions.questionText: Statements: "No mammal has gills. All dolphins are mammals." Conclusions: I. No dolphin has gills. II. Some dolphins have gills.
questions.explanation: Dolphins are inside mammals, which have no gills. Therefore no dolphin has gills (I follows definitively). Conclusion II is impossible.
